battle.name: 索馬利亞戰事 (2006年至2009年)
battle.brief: 索馬利亞戰事（2006年至2009年）主要發生於索馬利亞南部與摩加迪沙，過渡聯邦政府與反對武裝為控制首都、港口及國家政權而交戰。英國海軍的Steam ironclad於1865年列裝，是蒸汽動力鐵甲戰艦，屬早期遠洋艦隊骨幹。

kit.name: 蒸汽鐵甲艦
kit.history: Steam ironclad於1865年服役於英國皇家海軍，定位為蒸汽動力鐵甲戰艦，負責遠洋兵力投射、護航與海上作戰。

countries: 這場戰事的主軸，是索馬利亞過渡聯邦政府（TFG）及其外部支援者，對抗以索馬利亞伊斯蘭法院聯盟為基礎、後由青年黨（al-Shabaab）主導的聯盟武裝。2006年12月，埃塞俄比亞國家國防軍以「恢復希望行動」名義進入索馬利亞，與TFG共同奪取莫加迪沙和巴多阿；非洲聯盟駐索馬利亞使團（AMISOM）則由烏干達、布隆迪、肯亞等國部隊組成，在中部、南部若干城鎮守點並護路。主要戰線沿莫加迪沙、巴多阿、厄德海雷、拉斯坎博尼和基斯馬尤一帶展開；青年黨最終控制莫加迪沙與基斯馬尤，TFG仍保有巴多阿及部分南部據點。因此，這並非埃塞俄比亞與另一個國家之間的正面交戰，而是索馬利亞內部聯盟戰爭、國家軍介入與跨國安全部隊部署交疊形成的戰役。
countriesEn: The central axis of this conflict was the Somali Transitional Federal Government (TFG) and its external supporters fighting a coalition armed force based on the Somali Islamic Courts and later dominated by al-Shabaab. In December 2006, the Ethiopian National Defense Force entered Somalia under Operation Restore Hope and joined the TFG in taking Mogadishu and Baidoa. The African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM), composed principally of contingents from Uganda, Burundi, and Kenya, guarded selected towns and transport routes in central and southern Somalia. The principal front ran through Mogadishu, Baidoa, El Dhere, Ras Kamboni, and Kismayo. Al-Shabaab ultimately controlled Mogadishu and Kismayo, while the TFG retained Baidoa and several southern positions. This was therefore not a conventional interstate war between Ethiopia and another country, but an overlapping combination of a Somali coalition conflict, intervention by a national army, and deployment of multinational security forces.
people: 人物層面呈現三種彼此不完全一致的權力鏈。索馬利亞過渡聯邦政府主席阿卜杜拉·尤素福·艾哈邁德提供政治合法性，但各支武裝仍分別掌握兵員、車輛與地方資源；2006年12月介入開始時，內閣總理阿里·穆罕默德·蓋迪負責中央行政，實際戰鬥則分散在多支政府民兵及埃塞俄比亞部隊之間。埃塞俄比亞方面，後來出任總理的阿比亞·艾哈邁德當時是ENDF前線指揮官之一，率領部分先頭部隊進入莫加迪沙並參與巴多阿方向作戰；他的作用主要是組織有限目標的攻堅，而非決定索馬利亞全境政治。反方向的核心政治暨軍事領袖哈桑·達希爾·奧伊斯，曾領導伊斯蘭法院聯盟及後續聯盟組織，擅長把地方民兵、青年組織與城鎮防禦結合。AMISOM各國分遣隊則維持各自指揮鏈。這種指揮分散、互信有限而火力資源集中於少數正規部隊的結構，直接造成後續攻勢迅速展開、卻難以長期鞏固的矛盾。
peopleEn: Three incompletely integrated chains of authority shaped the conflict. TFG president Abdullahi Yusuf Ahmed provided political legitimacy, although individual factions continued to control their own troops, vehicles, and local resources. Prime minister Ali Mohamed Ghedi headed the civilian administration when the intervention began in December 2006, while combat power remained divided among several government militias and Ethiopian formations. On the Ethiopian side, Abiy Ahmed, later prime minister, was one of the ENDF's field commanders in 2006. He led elements of the vanguard into Mogadishu and fought in the Baidoa sector; his principal function was to direct operations against limited objectives rather than determine the political fate of all Somalia. Hassan Dahir Aweys was the principal political and military leader on the opposing coalition side, having led the Islamic Courts organization and its successor. He was effective at linking local militias, youth networks, and urban defenses. AMISOM contingents retained separate command chains. This combination of fragmented authority, limited mutual trust, and concentrated firepower among a few regular formations directly produced campaigns that began quickly but proved difficult to sustain.
kits: 截至2006年，埃塞俄比亞軍隊可投入南部作戰的主要裝備包括AKM與AK-47步槍、FN FAL七點六二公厘步槍、H&K G3步槍、PKM七點六二乘五十四公釐通用機槍、DShK十二點七乘一〇八公釐重機槍、2B14八一公釐迫擊砲，以及D-30一二二公釐榴彈砲。索馬利亞聯盟民兵則大量使用AKM、AK-47、PKM、DShK與RPG-7，技術車多以豐田Hilux底盤承擔巡邏、警戒和後送任務，手榴彈可見RGD-5等型號。相應的主要彈種包括七點六二乘三十九公釐、七點六二乘五十一北約、七點六二乘五十四俄式、十二點七乘一〇八公釐，以及八一公釐迫擊砲彈與一二二公釐榴彈砲彈。實戰中這批火器並非平均分配：FN FAL、G3、AK系列和PKM構成主要步兵火力，DShK提供超越及要點封鎖能力，2B14支撐小隊攻擊，D-30則須依賴較完整的道路、燃料與觀察條件；聯盟民兵雖能迅速集中RPG-7及輕機槍，卻較難維持同等後勤。上述型號均不晚於2006年，亦未把後來才大量出現的裝備倒置到本段戰事。
kitsEn: The principal equipment available to Ethiopian forces for southern operations by 2006 included AKM and AK-47 rifles, FN FAL 7.62 mm rifles, H&K G3 rifles, PKM 7.62×54 mm general-purpose machine guns, DShK 12.7×108 mm heavy machine guns, 2B14 81 mm mortars, and D-30 122 mm howitzers. Somali coalition militias relied extensively on AKM, AK-47, PKM, DShK, and RPG-7, with Toyota Hilux-based technical vehicles used for patrols, road security, and logistics. RGD-5 hand grenades were also available. The corresponding principal ammunition types included 7.62×39 mm, 7.62×51 mm NATO, 7.62×54 mm Russian, and 12.7×108 mm rounds, together with 81 mm mortar ammunition and 122 mm howitzer shells. These weapons were not evenly distributed in practice. FN FAL, G3, AK-pattern rifles, and PKMs formed the main infantry fire base; DShKs supplied heavier fire and blockade capability; 2B14 mortars supported platoon attacks; and D-30 howitzers depended on better roads, fuel supplies, and observation. Coalition militias could concentrate RPG-7s and light machine guns quickly but could not sustain equivalent logistics. All the listed models were fielded no later than 2006, and no later-generation equipment has been projected backward into this campaign.
tactics: 埃塞俄比亞軍的開局戰法建立在速度、縱深與道路控制上，而不是全面掃蕩鄉村。前進隊伍以車隊和戰術行軍姿態沿少數幹線推進，先控制交叉路口、城鎮外圍與補給點，再由工兵、警戒分隊及後勤車隊處理道路和障礙；抵達莫加迪沙後，聯軍優先奪取機場、港口、政府機關及主要街道，TFG民兵依地利引導搜索，ENDF以迫擊砲和機槍提供外圈火力。南下方向則以巴多阿為主要支點，經阿福戈耶、德爾維什一帶向拉斯坎博尼推進；前進過快、側翼拉長及後勤車隊暴露，使攻勢在拉斯坎博尼受到阻滯。青年黨民兵避免在失去縱深後固守整座城市，常以小股夜行、分散轉進、道路伏擊、RPG-7直射及迫擊砲襲擊消耗聯軍，必要時再退入預設陣地。聯軍後勤主要循吉吉加—戈德—巴多阿—莫加迪沙一線輸送，彈藥依口徑分批前送；遠距離砲兵與前線突擊因此始終受道路、燃料及護送能力限制。
tacticsEn: Ethiopian opening methods emphasized speed, depth, and control of roads rather than an exhaustive sweep of the countryside. Advance formations moved along a small number of trunk routes in motorized columns and tactical road march, first securing junctions, approaches to towns, and supply points. Engineers, security detachments, and logistics columns then dealt with roads and obstacles. At Mogadishu, the coalition prioritized the airport, the port, government installations, and principal streets. TFG militias exploited local knowledge to guide searches, while ENDF mortars and machine guns provided fire from the outer positions. The southern thrust used Baidoa as its main anchor and advanced through the Afgooye and Dervish area toward Ras Kamboni. Rapid movement, extended flanks, and exposed logistics columns contributed to the offensive's loss of momentum at Ras Kamboni. Al-Shabaab militias generally avoided prolonged defense of an entire city once its depth had been lost. They used small night movements, dispersed transfers, roadside ambushes, direct RPG-7 fire, and mortar attacks to wear down the coalition, withdrawing into prepared positions when necessary. Coalition logistics principally followed the Jijiga–Gode–Baidoa–Mogadishu axis, with ammunition moved forward by caliber and route. Long-range artillery and rapid infantry attacks therefore remained constrained by roads, fuel, and escort capacity.
data: 戰局可按日期重建。2006年6月，TFG在莫加迪沙失守後退往埃塞俄比亞；至11月初，TFG已控制基斯馬尤。12月5日，IGAD同意由埃塞俄比亞出兵並延長AMISOM部署；12月8日，聯合國安全理事會通過第1727號決議，延長AMISOM六個月授權；12月20日，ENDF開始越境。12月25日，聯軍進入莫加迪沙並控制機場、港口等核心設施；12月26日，TFG在埃軍支援下取得巴多阿，德爾維什方向的戰鬥隨即展開。2007年1月，聯軍沿沙貝萊河谷向厄德海雷及吉多方向推進，擴大南部控制區；3月9日至10日，TFG再攻莫加迪沙受挫；3月21日至23日拉斯坎博尼攻勢失敗，前線推進再度停滯。5月，聯軍一度重入莫加迪沙，但7月的聯盟反攻迫使TFG與ENDF再撤，主要埃軍於7月前後陸續退出索馬利亞。AMISOM則繼續駐守若干據點。2009年2月初，青年黨最終控制莫加迪沙；8月22日前後，聯盟攻取基斯馬尤，隨後控制胡杜爾一帶；11月，TFG在AMISOM配合下奪回胡杜爾及吉多部分據點，卻未能收復基斯馬尤，戰役至此仍沒有出現能扭轉全局的決定性會戰。
dataEn: The campaign can be reconstructed chronologically. In June 2006, the TFG was driven from Mogadishu and withdrew toward Ethiopia; by early November it controlled Kismayo. On 5 December, IGAD agreed to an Ethiopian deployment and an extension of AMISOM. On 8 December, United Nations Security Council Resolution 1727 extended AMISOM's mandate for six months. Ethiopian forces began crossing the border on 20 December. On 25 December, the coalition entered Mogadishu and secured the airport, the port, and other central facilities. On 26 December, TFG forces with Ethiopian support took Baidoa, followed by fighting in the Dervish sector. In January 2007, the coalition advanced along the Shabelle valley toward El Dhere and Gedo, enlarging its southern control zone. An offensive against Mogadishu on 9–10 March was repelled, and the failed attack at Ras Kamboni on 21–23 March halted the drive. The coalition briefly re-entered Mogadishu in May, but an al-Shabaab counteroffensive in July forced the TFG and ENDF to withdraw again, with the main Ethiopian units leaving during July. AMISOM retained several positions. By early February 2009, al-Shabaab secured full control of Mogadishu. Around 22 August it took Kismayo and subsequently occupied the Hudur sector. In November, TFG and AMISOM forces recaptured Hudur and several positions in Gedo but failed to recover Kismayo. No single decisive engagement had yet reversed the overall course of the campaign.
cause: 這場戰爭有明確的制度原因與直接原因。原有AMISOM授權接近屆滿，非盟部隊數量不足以同時守住莫加迪沙、中部城鎮與南部交通線；TFG雖有國際承認，卻缺乏統一指揮、有效裝甲和可持續補給，2006年6月失去莫加迪沙後更難自行奪回。IGAD因此在12月5日決定引進埃塞俄比亞部隊，並要求AMISOM繼續六個月；第1727號安全理事會決議則在延長非盟任務的同時，容許在與IGAD磋商框架下處理埃塞部署，但並非概括授權其後每一項戰鬥。埃塞俄比亞的直接考量包括阻止跨境的武裝網絡、降低青年黨及相關組織在邊境活動的威脅、保護既有合作關係，以及避免索馬利亞中部與南部形成無法控制的敵對區。青年黨控制莫加迪沙和南部要道，則使莫加迪沙—巴多阿—基斯馬尤走廊的爭奪成為雙方勝負關鍵。「恢復希望行動」因此兼具同盟援助、邊境安全與有限城市攻點三層目的。
causeEn: The conflict had both structural and immediate causes. The existing AMISOM mandate was approaching expiration, and African Union forces were too few to hold Mogadishu, central towns, and southern transport routes simultaneously. Although internationally recognized, the TFG lacked unified command, effective armor, and sustainable logistics; after losing Mogadishu in June 2006, it had little capacity to retake the capital alone. On 5 December, IGAD consequently decided to bring in Ethiopian troops and requested a six-month continuation of AMISOM. Security Council Resolution 1727 extended the African Union mission while allowing Ethiopian deployment to be handled through consultations with IGAD, but it did not constitute blanket authorization for every subsequent Ethiopian combat operation. Ethiopia's immediate concerns included preventing armed networks from crossing the border, reducing the threat posed by al-Shabaab and associated organizations, preserving established relationships, and avoiding the emergence of an uncontrolled hostile zone in central and southern Somalia. Because al-Shabaab controlled Mogadishu and major southern routes, competition over the Mogadishu–Baidoa–Kismayo corridor became decisive. Operation Restore Hope therefore combined alliance support, border security, and a limited effort to seize strategic urban objectives.
impact: 軍事影響首先表現在控制權的迅速翻轉。2006年12月占領莫加迪沙與巴多阿，使TFG在數週內取得南部補給基地和連接基斯馬尤的走廊，青年黨則退向中部、北部及預設陣地；短時間內，埃軍的集中兵力與道路機動速度明顯優於分散的聯盟民兵。但同一套機制也產生反作用：ENDF必須保護長距離車隊、城鎮外圍與南部據點，兵力越向前推，回援和補給越困難；2007年3月的莫加迪沙與拉斯坎博尼失利，顯示突進戰術不能替代持久清剿和地方控制。青年黨未被消滅，反而保留分散火力、熟悉道路的突擊組及城鎮民兵，並將其轉化為控制中部和南部公路網的常態兵力。AMISOM接手部分防務後仍只能守住有限據點，無法扭轉青年黨擴張。及至2009年，埃塞俄比亞已經退出，青年黨掌握莫加迪沙與基斯馬尤，TFG的南部根據地則縮小至巴多阿及吉多、拜州部分據點。
impactEn: The first military effect was a rapid reversal in control. Taking Mogadishu and Baidoa in December 2006 gave the TFG a southern supply base and a corridor toward Kismayo within weeks, while al-Shabaab withdrew into central, northern, and prepared positions. In the short term, the Ethiopian concentration of troops and speed along roads clearly exceeded the mobility of the dispersed coalition militias. The same system also produced the opposite effect. The ENDF had to protect long convoys, approaches to towns, and southern positions; the farther it advanced, the harder became reinforcement and resupply. The setbacks at Mogadishu and Ras Kamboni in March 2007 demonstrated that rapid penetration could not replace sustained clearing operations and effective local control. Al-Shabaab was not destroyed. It retained dispersed firepower, road-oriented strike groups, and urban militias, converting them into a standing force capable of controlling the central and southern road network. After AMISOM assumed part of the defense, it still held only a limited number of positions and could not reverse al-Shabaab's expansion. By 2009, Ethiopian forces had departed, al-Shabaab held Mogadishu and Kismayo, and the TFG's southern foothold had contracted to Baidoa and parts of Gedo and Bay.
result: 截至2009年底，戰略結果明顯有利於青年黨，但雙方經歷的是一系列勝負互見的戰役，而非某一場會戰決定一切。埃塞俄比亞初期依靠集中兵力、準確瞄準莫加迪沙與巴多阿等交通樞紐，獲得了速度上的勝利；然而聯軍未能把短期占領轉化為能覆蓋城鎮、道路和後勤網的常態控制，2007年的反攻與撤退遂使這項優勢逐漸流失。TFG仍控制巴多阿，並在2009年11月配合AMISOM奪回胡杜爾及部分吉多據點，顯示聯盟仍具有限攻勢能力；但莫加迪沙與基斯馬尤已落入青年黨，埃塞俄比亞主力也早已離境，因此原先保障TFG的南方通道實際上被切斷。關於雙方總傷亡，公開資料彼此矛盾且缺乏可核對的完整名冊，本實錄不引用未經證實的精確數字。2009年結束時，青年黨掌握兩項全國性樞紐，TFG與AMISOM退守若干據點，而索馬利亞戰爭仍未終止。
resultEn: By the end of 2009, the strategic balance clearly favored al-Shabaab, although the campaign consisted of a sequence of mixed successes and defeats rather than one decisive battle. Ethiopia initially used concentrated forces and precise objectives at Mogadishu, Baidoa, and other transport hubs to win a contest of speed. It could not convert that temporary occupation into permanent control of towns, roads, and the logistics network, so the advantage gradually disappeared during the 2007 counteroffensive and withdrawal. The TFG still held Baidoa and, in November 2009, recaptured Hudur and several positions in Gedo with AMISOM support, demonstrating a limited ability to conduct counteroffensives. Mogadishu and Kismayo, however, were under al-Shabaab control, while the main Ethiopian force had already left, effectively severing the southern corridor originally supporting the TFG. Public casualty totals from both sides are contradictory and lack verifiable complete records, so this account does not cite unconfirmed precise figures. At the end of 2009, al-Shabaab held two national pivots, the TFG and AMISOM retained a number of smaller positions, and the Somali war had not ended.
